title: API 580 Training in Salt Lake City: Risk-Based Inspection Prep
description: Self-paced API 580 exam prep for Salt Lake City RBI planners and integrity engineers: Utah vessel rules, PSM, crude slate changes. Instructor Q&A.
h1: API 580 Training in Salt Lake City: Risk-Based Inspection Exam Prep for Inspection Planners, Integrity Engineers and Inspectors at Wasatch Front Refineries
html:
API 580 exam prep for risk-based inspection work in the Salt Lake valley

Utah's five refineries sit within a few miles of each other in Salt Lake City, North Salt Lake and Woods Cross, and each one decides how often to inspect thousands of pieces of equipment. Increasingly that decision is documented through risk-based inspection: a structured look at what can go wrong with each item, how likely it is and how bad it would be. API 580 is the certification for people who take part in that work, and its exam is built on the API 580 Body of Knowledge, which draws on API RP 580.

This page is for inspection planners, corrosion and reliability engineers, inspection supervisors and experienced inspectors in the valley who want to sit API 580. It explains where RBI sits in Utah's regulatory picture, why the local crude slate makes reassessment a live issue, what data a Salt Lake RBI team works from, and how to prepare for a closed-book paper. There is no Atlantis classroom in Salt Lake City. The course is online and self-paced, and an instructor answers your questions as you go.

Who sits API 580 at a Salt Lake refinery

API 580 suits people whose job touches the inspection plan rather than only the inspection. At a typical refinery that means:

  • the inspection planner or RBI coordinator who maintains the risk ranking and the due dates it produces;
  • corrosion, materials and reliability engineers who carry out the damage mechanism review and set corrosion rates;
  • certified API 510, API 570 and API 653 inspectors who supply findings and judge inspection effectiveness;
  • process engineers who own the operating limits that keep damage mechanisms in check;
  • inspection contractors and consultants who run RBI studies for owners.

Anyone already holding a current API 510, 570 or 653 certificate meets the API 580 eligibility rules without further evidence. Others qualify through education plus petrochemical industry experience within the last ten years: one year with a bachelor's degree, two with a two-year degree or certificate, three with a high school diploma, and five or more without formal education. The exam has 90 multiple-choice questions, 80 scored and 10 unscored pretest items, answered closed-book in 3.25 hours.

The mechanical integrity frame: PSM under Utah's State Plan

Utah runs its own occupational safety programme. The Utah Occupational Safety and Health Division, part of the Labor Commission, administers the state plan, which covers private sector as well as state and local government workplaces, from a single office in Salt Lake City. Its general rule incorporates the federal general industry standards from 29 CFR 1910.21 to the end of Part 1910, in the 2024 edition, which takes in the process safety management standard at 1910.119.

The mechanical integrity element of that standard requires inspection and testing of process equipment to follow recognised and generally accepted good engineering practices, at a frequency consistent with manufacturers' recommendations and good engineering practice, and more often where operating experience shows it is needed. It does not require RBI. What RBI gives a Salt Lake refinery is a documented, defensible answer to the question an auditor asks about each frequency: why this interval, for this item, in this service?

When an RBI result meets Utah's vessel rules

An RBI study can recommend an interval; it cannot rewrite a regulation. Two sets of rules bound what an RBI result can do in the valley.

  • The state's boiler and pressure vessel rule. Utah Administrative Code R616-2-8 puts vessels under the Labor Commission's jurisdiction on a fixed cycle: 24 months for heat exchangers on high-pressure steam or high-temperature water and for autoclaves above 15 psi steam, and 48 months for every other vessel. A business holding an owner/user certificate may inspect its own unfired pressure vessels with its own certified agents, but under procedures and frequencies the division establishes. An owner who wants RBI-based frequencies for jurisdictional vessels therefore has to work them through the division's owner/user framework, not around it.
  • Federal breakout tank rules. Where a pipeline operator's atmospheric or low-pressure steel breakout tanks are involved, 49 CFR 195.432(b) requires inspection to API Standard 653 except section 6.4.3, the alternative internal inspection interval through which an RBI assessment would otherwise set the internal interval. PHMSA published a proposal in June 2026 that would allow RBI-based intervals for breakout tanks with upper limits, but at the time of writing it was a proposal, not a rule.

A plant-wide RBI programme in Utah is therefore a patchwork: refinery-owned equipment governed by the owner's programme and PSM, jurisdictional vessels inside the state cycle, and any pipeline tanks under federal rules. None of that patchwork is examined, but it shows why an RBI programme has to state its scope and boundaries clearly, and the RBI programme is one of the topic areas the current Body of Knowledge lists.

The crude slate as an RBI input

Salt Lake refineries run an unusually varied diet. Marathon says its refinery processes crude from Utah, Colorado, Wyoming and Canada. The Frontier Aspen pipeline from Casper, Wyoming, supplies Canadian and Rocky Mountain crudes to the area's refiners. Waxy crude from the Uinta Basin arrives by insulated truck, and market analysts describe its black wax and yellow wax grades as low in sulfur, acid and metals. HF Sinclair says its Woods Cross refinery has access to regional sweet and waxy crudes and, by pipeline, to Canadian crude.

For an RBI team that variety is the main reason a risk ranking goes stale. The probability of failure for a crude unit overhead, a hot crude transfer line or a vacuum column depends on the corrosivity of what is being processed, and a shift in the proportion of each crude moves corrosion rates in different directions in different parts of the plant. RP 580 treats a change in process conditions or feedstock as a reason to reassess, and integrity operating windows on sulfur, acid content and temperature are the practical way a site notices the change before the inspection data does.

Consequence in a valley of shared pipelines

Consequence of failure in RP 580 covers safety and health, environmental damage and financial loss, including the cost of lost production. The financial side has a local shape here. HF Sinclair says Woods Cross products are sold mainly in Utah, Idaho, Nevada, Wyoming and eastern Washington. The UNEV pipeline carries products south from Woods Cross to Cedar City and the Las Vegas valley, and the Salt Lake products system runs north to Burley, Pocatello, Boise and Pasco. A long unplanned outage at one plant in a five-refinery valley that supplies several states through a handful of pipelines is a consequence an RBI team can quantify through business interruption, and it can move equipment up the ranking even where the safety consequence is modest.

The safety and environmental consequence for a given release still depends on the fluid, the inventory that can escape, the detection and isolation available and the people and receptors nearby. Those are site-specific inputs, and the exam tests how they combine rather than any particular plant's values.

Data a Salt Lake RBI team works from

An RBI assessment is only as good as the data behind it. A Salt Lake team typically assembles:

  1. design and construction records, including materials, design conditions and any rerating;
  2. inspection history: CML thickness readings, internal inspection reports, NDT results and the effectiveness of each past inspection against the damage expected;
  3. a damage mechanism review for each corrosion loop, using API RP 571 as the reference;
  4. process data and integrity operating window records, including crude slate history;
  5. state inspection records, such as each jurisdictional vessel's Certificate of Inspection and Permit to Operate and reports from insurers' deputy inspectors;
  6. boundary documents showing where refinery piping and tanks meet pipeline company equipment.

Gaps in that list do not stop an assessment, but they lower confidence in the probability of failure. RP 580 expects an RBI programme to recognise uncertainty, and the idea that an effective inspection reduces risk by reducing uncertainty about the equipment's condition runs through the whole document.

A closed-book exercise: a crude preheat train after a crude switch

Work through this scenario the way the exam expects you to reason, without numbers. A Salt Lake crude unit has run for several years on a slate dominated by low-sulfur waxy crude. Its preheat exchangers and the hot transfer line to the furnace rank medium risk, with inspection due dates set from steady corrosion rates. The refinery now plans to raise the share of pipeline crude, and assume for this exercise that the new blend carries more sulfur.

  1. Does the probability of failure change? Yes, potentially. Higher sulfur at high temperature can raise sulfidation rates in the hot end, so the corrosion rates behind the current ranking may no longer hold.
  2. Should the team wait for the next scheduled reassessment? No. A feedstock change is a trigger for reassessment, and the damage mechanism review for the affected loops should be revisited first.
  3. Does the consequence change? Not necessarily. The fluid's flammability, the inventory and the surroundings are largely the same, so the change shows up mainly on the probability axis of the risk matrix.
  4. What reduces the risk? Inspection does not change the damage rate; it reduces uncertainty about it. An early, effective thickness survey on the hot end confirms the new rate, while operating limits on sulfur and temperature reduce the likelihood of damage itself.

Keep those last two ideas apart when you answer practice questions: in RP 580's terms, inspection lowers the uncertainty about damage, not the likelihood that the damage occurs.

Preparing for a closed-book RBI paper

API 580 has no open-book half, so preparation is about understanding and recall. The 2026 Body of Knowledge lists a single publication, API RP 580, fourth edition (2023) with its 2025 addendum, arranged in ten topic areas that run from risk assessment and data collection through damage mechanisms, probability and consequence of failure and risk management to RBI documentation. Learn the vocabulary of RP 580 precisely: risk, probability of failure, consequence of failure, risk targets, inspection effectiveness, mitigation and reassessment. Practise reading a risk matrix and explaining why an item sits where it does. Know the difference between qualitative, semi-quantitative and quantitative approaches, and remember that API RP 581 is the quantitative method rather than the subject of the exam. Damage mechanisms appear as reasoning questions: which mechanism is plausible in a given service, and which inspection method would detect it.

The course lets you work at your own pace through those topics, with practice questions and timed papers set to the real exam's length. When a practice answer seems to contradict RP 580's wording, send the question; the instructor answers from the text so you see how the exam setter is reading it.

Exam preparation or an RBI study for your plant?

The two are different services. The exam-prep course prepares individuals to sit API 580 and to work competently on an RBI team. An owner that needs a study carried out on its own equipment needs something else, and Atlantis also carries out remote RBI studies for owners, working from the data the owner provides. Fitness-for-service assessment is a separate discipline that Atlantis does not offer.

Sponsoring API 580 candidates from Salt Lake employers

Refiners in the valley, their inspection contractors and engineering firms can enrol one candidate or a whole RBI team, and fees are quoted on request. Sponsoring the planner, the corrosion engineer and an inspector together gives a team a shared vocabulary before it reassesses a unit. Each candidate applies to API individually, and API administers the exam and issues the certification.

faq.q: Do I need API 510, API 570 or API 653 before I can take API 580?
faq.a: No. Holding one of them is simply the quickest route, because current holders automatically qualify. Without one, you qualify through education and petrochemical industry experience within the last ten years: one year with a bachelor's degree, two with a two-year degree or certificate, three with a high school diploma, or five or more without formal education. Engineers at Salt Lake refineries usually meet this through their own work.

faq.q: Does Utah's state OSHA plan require refineries to use RBI?
faq.a: No. Utah's plan incorporates the federal process safety management standard, whose mechanical integrity element requires inspection and testing that follows recognised good engineering practice at appropriate frequencies. RBI is one way an owner can show how its frequencies were chosen and why they suit each item, but the standard does not prescribe it.

faq.q: Can an RBI study lengthen the 48-month state inspection cycle on a Utah pressure vessel?
faq.a: Not on its own authority. Rule R616-2-8 sets the state cycle, and owner/user agencies inspect their own unfired vessels under procedures and frequencies the division establishes. An owner who wants RBI-based frequencies for jurisdictional vessels needs to work through the division. For equipment outside the state's jurisdiction, the owner's programme and PSM govern.

faq.q: I work in operations at a Woods Cross refinery. Does that count toward API 580?
faq.a: API frames API 580 eligibility as education plus petrochemical industry experience within the last ten years, rather than the inspection agency experience the other three programmes ask for. Refinery operations is petrochemical industry experience, but API verifies each application, so describe your duties accurately. Operators often make strong RBI team members because they know how the plant actually runs.

faq.q: Our crude slate changes through the year. How often should our RBI be reassessed?
faq.a: RP 580 expects reassessment when something material changes, such as feedstock, operating conditions, a newly identified damage mechanism or unexpected inspection findings, as well as at the interval your programme sets. In a valley where refineries switch between waxy, Rocky Mountain and Canadian crudes, integrity operating windows help decide when a change is material enough to trigger it.

faq.q: Will the API 580 exam ask about Utah's boiler rules or the PSM standard?
faq.a: No. The current API 580 Body of Knowledge is built on one publication, API RP 580, and neither Utah's Rule R616-2 nor the text of the PSM standard appears in it. What the exam does test is the reasoning RP 580 sets out for a programme that has to operate within whatever rules apply, from data collection and damage mechanisms to risk management and documentation. Local rules shape how your programme runs at work; RP 580 is what you are examined on.

faq.q: Is API 580 useful for an NDT technician?
faq.a: It can be, particularly for technicians moving towards inspection planning. RBI depends on judging how effective a given inspection method is against a given damage mechanism, which is everyday knowledge for an experienced technician. Atlantis's NDT training in Salt Lake City covers the ASNT SNT-TC-1A methods; API 580 adds the planning side.

faq.q: Can our refinery put its whole RBI team through API 580 preparation?
faq.a: Yes. A refinery or contractor can enrol several people, and fees are quoted on request. Each candidate works at their own pace and puts their own questions to the instructor, so planners, engineers and inspectors on different schedules can prepare together for the same exam window. Each person still applies to API separately.
